milestone: Internal physics identity ownership and topology rollback foundation
implemented: Runtime inventories and seals all startup physics body identities, including Character bodies.
Internal value-copy allocator uses lowest available slots, exact ownership checks and nonwrapping generations.
Committed generation 255 retirement exhausts that slot; there are 4096 physical slots. No unlimited lifetime allocation claim.

Linux.method: CMake single-job build; three CTest invocations, two tests each.

Windows.method: CMake LLVM-MinGW single-job build; native Windows execution via Windows Python.

topology_checks: Automatic startup bodies are inventoried before exclusive explicit-ID allocation.
Active and sleeping cohorts each restore exact body state and serialized checkpoint bytes after three speculative remove/create/simulate batches.
Each positive cohort matches motion and sorted contact-event kinds/body pairs for 270 continuation ticks and 120 further ticks after a new committed creation.
Automatic-ID negative control confirms failed creation batches consume future identities.
Extra-body negative control confirms RestoreState success does not establish correct body membership.

limitations: Runtime entity/component membership is still fixed; no public spawn/despawn API is implemented by this change.
The topology fixture exercises rigid boxes with contact and sleep state, not dynamic Characters, constraints, mesh creation or production ECS structural journals.
Continuation is compared within each OS/build; no arbitrary cross-platform bit-exact guarantee.
Allocator checkpoints must be restored together with actual physical membership. Retired body slots may be released only after Jolt allocation destruction.
Portable saves still reconstruct physics caches; this internal rollback test does not strengthen portable-save determinism guarantees.
These are functional tests on the development laptop, not throughput or battery-performance measurements. Existing desktop package was not republished.
